newsitem.title: USA: L.A. anti-terror police arrest "militia" members.
newsitem.headline: L.A. anti-terror police arrest "militia" members.

text.p: Los Angeles anti-terrorist police on Friday arrested five members of a "militia cell" and seized grenades, automatic weapons and thousands of rounds of ammunition, authorities said.
The Los Angeles Police Department said in a statement that the arrests were the culmination of a two-year investigation that started after the Oklahoma City bombing in April 1995.
Five men were arrested in a series of early-morning raids by the LAPD's Anti-Terrorist Division, it said.
They were charged with weapons violations, including possession and/or sales of fully automatic assault weapons.

Property seized at four separate locations included a grenade launcher, hand grenades, hand grenade components, automatic assault rifles, body armor, ballistic helmets, night vision goggles, thousands of rounds of ammunition and over 100 different types of weapons.

The police identified the five arrested as Glenn Yee, a reserve police officer in the city of Irwindale, Alvin Ung, Mark Grand, Timothy Swanson and Raymond Durand. They were said to belong to a "local militia cell", but police declined any further comment.
